contrasts.dialect: Contemporary Standard Russian; isolated stressed citation words
contrasts.label: Ы and и: stressed vowel sounds
contrasts.rationale: A pedagogically important sound comparison omitted from the first pack. Non-native perception research directly examines this sound distinction.
contextNotes: All words are stressed monosyllables; do not mix reduced unstressed vowels into these categories.
IPA is broad and editorial. It omits predictable narrow coarticulation; exact audio must be reviewed later.
targetOccurrence is 1-based among exact targetSegment occurrences. Every listed word has exactly one vowel nucleus.
The first pool has plain onsets; the second has palatalized onsets. This shared group explicitly represents the coupled pattern, not identical consonantal context.
Five-vowel analyses often treat [ɨ] as conditioned relative to /i/; six-vowel analyses give it separate status. The lesson must not resolve that debate by fiat.
Мыл/мил and был/бил are useful linked examples, but both onset softness and vowel realization change; neither is entered as a vowel-only minimal pair.
Быть/бить has the same issue and is intentionally not used as proof of a one-vowel lexical contrast.
reviewNotes: Contrast-first review only. If the intended outcome is vowel-only perception, ordinary whole-word ABX can be solved using onset softness and cannot demonstrate that outcome.
Decide whether to keep a combined consonant-plus-vowel lesson or later develop a separately validated vowel-only task. No clipping or new audio has been performed.

Сын and рис have individual Gramota dictionary support for their lexical senses and spellings, inspected through indexed primary entries; their broad IPA and eventual recordings remain review-required.
contrasts.scopeNote: This compares the sounds [ɨ] and [i]. In these words the preceding consonant also changes from hard to soft, so these are not vowel-only minimal pairs.

contrasts.label: Stressed и and е after a soft consonant
contrasts.rationale: Separates two front vowels while keeping preceding consonants palatalized in both categories.
contextNotes: All words are stressed monosyllables; do not mix reduced unstressed vowels into these categories.
IPA is broad and editorial. It omits predictable narrow coarticulation; exact audio must be reviewed later.
targetOccurrence is 1-based among exact targetSegment occurrences. Every listed word has exactly one vowel nucleus.
Unlike the ы/и pool, both categories have a soft onset and a plain coda; do not add hard-onset loanwords with э without a separate group.
Broad /e/ can be phonetically more open in this context; the category symbol is not a claim of one invariant narrow vowel.
Do not substitute мёл (swept) for мел (chalk).

contextNotes: All words are stressed monosyllables; do not mix reduced unstressed vowels into these categories.
IPA is broad and editorial. It omits predictable narrow coarticulation; exact audio must be reviewed later.

The phonetic contrast remains teachable whether [ɨ] is analyzed as a separate phoneme or a context-conditioned realization.
Both categories use plain consonants; this group does not require the onset-softness switch present in ы/и.
reviewNotes: Мул is explicitly documented in the Gramota stressed-vowel examples. Бук now has an individual Gramota dictionary reference for the beech-tree sense, inspected through indexed primary entries.
No universal L1 difficulty ranking is asserted; personal diagnostics should determine priority.
contrasts.scopeNote: A stressed vowel-sound comparison in plain-consonant contexts; the separate-phoneme status of [ɨ] is analysis-dependent.

gaps: Coverage correction: this addition introduces four Russian vowel comparisons; the previous pack already contains stressed o/u. Together they cover six pedagogical sound categories a, e, i, o, u, ɨ across five selected comparisons, not all pairwise combinations.

Remaining six-category pairwise inventory: a/e, a/i, a/ɨ, a/u, e/ɨ, e/o, e/u, i/o, i/u, ɨ/o. This is a coverage map, not a recommendation to create ten equally important lessons. Context compatibility and learner evidence must determine selection.
Unstressed reduction and stress movement need separate material: a/o neutralization and front-vowel reduction cannot be addressed by adding unstressed spellings to stressed categories.
Soft-consonant versus hard-consonant realizations of a, o, u and e remain additional contextual gaps; the sound category often changes its phonetic realization with its neighbours.
Russian letter pairs а/я, о/ё, у/ю, э/е are not automatically independent vowel-phoneme contrasts. Palatalization, jotation and position must be separated.

The ы/и sound distinction is pedagogically important despite its disputed phonemic analysis. Whole-word results from the supplied coupled pool cannot isolate vowel learning from onset-softness learning.
No claim that any new word appeared in an L2 stimulus table: all stimulusSourceIds are empty. No speech has been generated, downloaded for practice, or perceptually validated.

The seven follow-up lemmas сын, рис, сам, сом, там, том and бук now have individually inspected indexed Gramota dictionary entries. Complete IPA and owner word review remain pending; this draft is not deployable curriculum and does not certify recordings.
